'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#d2b1d9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} {{legend0|#909090|No data}} | title = U.S. senator | before_election = [[Pat Toomey]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[John Fetterman]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{Elections in Pennsylvania sidebar}} The '''2022 United States Senate election in Pennsylvania''' was held on November 8, 2022, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the [[Pennsylvania|Commonwealth of Pennsylvania]].{{cite news |last1=Levy |first1=Marc |title=Democrat John Fetterman wins US Senate race in Pennsylvania |url=https://apnews.com/article/pennsylvania-senate-race-2022-midterm-elections-93709b5b7ab4cef658f45751cd76c090 |access-date=November 10, 2022 |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 9, 2022}} [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] lieutenant governor [[John Fetterman]] defeated [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] surgeon [[Mehmet Oz]] to win his first term in office. Fetterman succeeded Republican incumbent [[Pat Toomey]], who did not seek re-election to a third term. This was the only U.S. Senate seat to flip parties in [[2022 United States elections|2022]]. In the May 17 primary, Fetterman won the Democratic nomination with 59% of the vote over Representative [[Conor Lamb]] and state Representative [[Malcolm Kenyatta]].{{cite web |title=Pennsylvania Senate Democratic Primary Election Results and Maps 2022 {{!}} CNN Politics |url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2022/results/pennsylvania/democratic-primaries/senate |access-date=2022-06-04 |website=CNN |language=en}} Oz finished with a 0.1% margin ahead of businessman [[Dave McCormick]] in the Republican primary, triggering an automatic recount. McCormick conceded the nomination on June 3,{{cite news |first=Eric |last=Bradner |title=Dave McCormick concedes Pennsylvania Senate GOP primary to Trump-backed Mehmet Oz |website=CNN |url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/06/03/politics/dave-mccormick-concedes-mehmet-oz-pennsylvania-senate-republican-primary/index.html |access-date=2022-06-04}} making Oz the first [[Islam in the United States|Muslim]] candidate to be nominated by either major party for U.S. Senate.{{cite news|last=Hammond|first=Joseph|title=Celebrity surgeon Dr. Oz seeks to be first Muslim elected to the US Senate|url=https://religionnews.com/2021/12/02/celebrity-surgeon-dr-oz-seeks-to-be-first-muslim-elected-to-the-u-s-senate/|work=Religion News|date=2 December 2021}} As the only open Republican-held Senate seat in a state won by [[Joe Biden]] in the [[2020 United States presidential election|2020 presidential election]], the race was among the most competitive of the 2022 midterms and characterized as highly contentious. Fetterman framed Oz as an [[elitism|elitist]] [[carpetbagger]] with a radical [[anti-abortion]] stance in the wake of ''[[Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization]]'' overturning ''[[Roe v. Wade]]'', while Oz framed Fetterman as a [[socialist]] insufficiently committed to fighting crime. Fetterman's health was also a major issue due to him suffering a stroke days before his primary victory.{{cite magazine|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/news/2022/11/john-fetterman-wins-pennsylvania-senate-race|title=John Fetterman Wins Pennsylvania Senate Race|magazine=Vanity Fair|last1=Tracy|first1=Abigail|date=November 9, 2022|accessdate=November 9, 2022}} Although Fetterman led most pre-election polls, concerns towards his health and a scrutinized debate performance helped Oz take a narrow lead before the election.{{Cite web |last=Manchester |first=Julia |date=2022-11-03 |title=Oz passes Fetterman for first time after Pennsylvania debate: poll |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/3716038-oz-passes-fetterman-for-first-time-in-post-debate-pennsylvania-poll/ |access-date=2022-11-30 |website=The Hill |language=en-US}}{{cite web|title=2022 Senate Election Forecast|date=June 30, 2022 |url=https://projects.fivethirtyeight.com/2022-election-forecast/senate/pennsylvania/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220630150635/https://projects.fivethirtyeight.com/2022-election-forecast/senate/pennsylvania/|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 30, 2022}}{{cite web|title=Battle for Senate|url=https://www.realclearpolitics.com/epolls/2022/senate/elections-map-rcp-projection.html}} Despite Oz's lead in final polls, Fetterman won by a 4.9% margin, helping provide Senate Democrats a net gain of one seat and their first outright majority since 2015. With Fetterman's victory, elected Democrats held both U.S. Senate seats from Pennsylvania for the first time since 1947.{{efn|Democrats held both of Pennsylvania's Senate seats from 2009 to 2011 when [[Arlen Specter]], who was elected as a Republican, switched to the Democratic Party.}} ==Republican primary== [[File:McCormick Portrait (HR) (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Former [[Under Secretary of the Treasury for International Affairs|U.S. Treasury Under Secretary]] and future U.S. Senator [[David McCormick]] narrowly lost the primary, placing second.]] [[File:Kathy Barnette headshot (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Author [[Kathy Barnette]] finished third in the primary.]] [[File:Carla Sands official photo (alt crop).jpg|thumb|upright|Former [[U.S. Ambassador to Denmark]] [[Carla Sands]] finished fourth in the primary.]] [[File:AmbBartos headshot 6-300x294.jpg|thumb|upright|Businessman [[Jeff Bartos]] finished fifth in the primary.]] [[File:George Bochetto on the Sam Lesante Show (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Former Pennsylvania Boxing Commissioner George Bochetto finished seventh in the primary.]] ===Campaign=== ====Early campaign==== In October 2020, incumbent Republican Senator [[Pat Toomey]] decided not to run for re-election, stating that he wished to return to the private sector.{{cite web|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2020/10/05/politics/pat-toomey-announcement-not-running-senate-pennsylvania/index.html|title=GOP Sen. Pat Toomey of Pennsylvania won't run for reelection in 2022|website=CNN|last1=Rogers|first1=Alex|date=October 5, 2020|access-date=December 1, 2021}} By October 2021, businessman [[Jeff Bartos]], who had posted strong fund-raising totals, and veteran [[Sean Parnell (spokesperson)|Sean Parnell]], who had the endorsement of former president [[Donald Trump]], emerged as the race's front-runners.{{Cite news|last=Olson|first=Tyler|date=October 14, 2021|title=GOP Pennsylvania Senate candidate Bartos touts war chest against Trump-backed opponent Parnell|url=https://www.foxnews.com/politics/bartos-fundraising-parnell-3rd-quarter-pennsylvania|website=Fox News|access-date=November 5, 2021}} However, Parnell's campaign faced a large scandal in November 2021, after his ex-wife, Laurie Snell, testified in court during a custody hearing for the couple's children that Parnell had strangled and spat on her, abused their children, and told her to "go get an abortion".{{Cite magazine|last=Wade|first=Pete|date=November 5, 2021|title=Trump Holding Massive Fund-Raiser for Senate Candidate Who Was Just Accused of Strangling His Wife|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/politics/politics-news/sean-parnell-trump-fundraiser-1253942/|magazine=Rolling Stone|access-date=November 5, 2021}} Parnell denied the allegations under oath. Even before these allegations were made, doubts had arisen among Republicans regarding Parnell's fundraising ability, and it became widely assumed that he would suspend his campaign if he did not win custody of his children.{{cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/newsletters/playbook/2021/11/09/a-trump-backed-senate-hopeful-takes-the-stand-495028|title=Politico Playbook: A Trump-backed Senate hopeful takes the stand|website=Politico|last1=Palmeri|first1=Tara|last2=Daniels|first2=Eugene|last3=Lizza|first3=Ryan|last4=Bade|first4=Rachael|date=November 9, 2021|access-date=November 30, 2021}}{{failed verification|date=August 2023}} On November 22, 2021, Snell was given custody of the couple's children and Parnell suspended his campaign. ====Entry of Oz and McCormick==== On November 30, with Parnell out of the race, [[Mehmet Oz]], a [[celebrity doctor]] and television personality, announced his candidacy.{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2021/11/30/dr-mehmet-oz-announces-senate-run/|title=Celebrity doctor Mehmet Oz announces Senate run in Pennsylvania, joins GOP field|newspaper=The Washington Post|last1=Wang|first1=Amy B.|last2=Sonmez|first2=Felicia|date=November 30, 2021|access-date=November 30, 2021}} Oz's campaign entered an immediate controversy over whether Oz himself was a resident of Pennsylvania, as he had lived in [[Cliffside Park, New Jersey]], for most of his life and had only registered to vote in Pennsylvania in October 2020.{{cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2021/11/30/dr-oz-announces-senate-bid-523530|title=Dr. Oz announces Senate bid to his millions of followers|website=Politico|last1=Allison|first1=Natalie|last2=Otterbein|first2=Holly|date=November 30, 2021|access-date=November 30, 2021}} The January 2022 entrance of [[David McCormick]], a businessman, into the race prompted attacks for McCormick's past detraction of Trump and criticism of "[[America First (policy)|America First]]" economic policies from Oz allies. [[Super PAC]]s allied to McCormick hit back with a spate of well-funded television advertisements, accusing Oz of being a "Hollywood liberal."{{cite web|url=https://whyy.org/articles/millions-pouring-into-pa-governor-and-u-s-senate-races-with-fetterman-and-oz-ahead/|title=Millions pouring into Pa. governor and U.S. Senate races, with Fetterman and Oz ahead|website=WHYY|last1=Meyer|first1=Katie|date=February 1, 2022|access-date=February 2, 2022}} Republican straw polls in January 2022 indicated strong support for Bartos and political commentator [[Kathy Barnette]] among party activists as the campaign started to escalate. Bartos won the Republican State Committee Central Caucus's straw poll, placing first with 49 votes, while Barnette finished in second place with 30 votes. McCormick and Sands trailed at third and fourth place; and Oz and former Boxing Commissioner George Bochetto performed poorly, each receiving only one vote.{{cite web|title=White, Bartos win GOP straw polls for governor, Senate, respectively|url=https://www.cityandstatepa.com/content/white-bartos-win-gop-straw-polls-governor-senate-respectively|website=City & State PA|last1=Sweitzer|first1=Justin|date=January 18, 2022}}{{cite web|title=Dr. Oz stumbles out of the gate in Senate race|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2022/01/25/dr-oz-senate-race-stumbles-00002056|access-date=January 31, 2022|date=January 25, 2022|last1=Otterbein|first1=Holly|website=Politico}} Despite this, political commentators largely considered Oz and McCormick to be the frontrunners, with the other candidates trailing them.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/04/25/us/politics/mehmet-oz-dave-mccormick-senate.html|title=Front-Runners in G.O.P. Pennsylvania Senate Race Are Put on Spot at Debate|website=The New York Times|last1=Epstein|first1=Reid J.|date=April 25, 2022|accessdate=November 11, 2022}} The McCormick campaign targeted Oz's ties to Turkey and called on him to renounce his Turkish citizenship, accusing Oz of harboring dual loyalties.{{Cite news |last=Goldmacher |first=Shane |date=2022-03-18 |title=Dr. Oz's Heritage Is Targeted as Rivals Vie for Trump Backing |language=en-US |newspaper=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/03/18/us/politics/dr-oz-trump-mccormick-senators-race.html |access-date=2022-03-24 |issn=0362-4331}} Oz later stated that if he were elected to the Senate, he would renounce his Turkish citizenship.{{cite web |last=Axelrod |first=Tal |date=March 16, 2022 |title=Oz says he will renounce Turkish citizenship if elected to Senate |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/598515-oz-says-he-will-renounce-turkish-citizenship-if-elected-to-senate |access-date=March 24, 2022 |website=The Hill |language=en}} Former president Trump endorsed Oz on April 10, citing the popularity of his television show and perceived appeal to female voters.{{cite magazine|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/news/2022/04/trump-endorses-dr-oz|title=Trump Endorses Dr. Oz, Citing His Popularity on TV and Nice Things he Said About Trump's Health|last1=Klein|first1=Charlotte|magazine=Vanity Fair|date=April 10, 2022|access-date=May 7, 2022}} Oz frequently highlighted this endorsement, it becoming one of his major talking points during the campaign. ====Late campaign==== Oz had been ahead of the other candidates in the polls since the start of his campaign, with McCormick soon rising quickly in the polls to challenge Oz, with both men polling the low 20s. Barnette had also begun to rise in the polls at this point after a string of attention-getting debate performances and an ad spend in support of her by the [[Club for Growth]]. Her late surge prompted a change in tactics from the two frontrunners, who had largely ignored her as irrelevant until then. Pro-Oz Super PAC American Leadership Action launched an ad campaign accusing Barnette of supporting [[Black Lives Matter]], while McCormick stated that Barnette was unelectable, citing her heavy loss in a U.S. House race the previous election cycle.{{cite web|last1 = Otterbein| first1= Holly| last2 = Allison| first2 = Natalie| title = GOP launches Operation Stop Barnette|work = [[Politico]]|date=May 12, 2022|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2022/05/12/gop-launches-operation-stop-barnette-00032303| access-date = May 13, 2022}} Oz himself also accused Barnette of [[Islamophobia]], pointing to a 2015 tweet in which she stated, "Pedophilia is a Cornerstone of Islam."{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/news/campaign/3488709-reprehensible-oz-condemns-gop-opponents-tweet-on-islam/|title='Reprehensible': Oz condemns GOP opponent's tweet on Islam|website=The in the primary.]] ===Campaign=== The first two major Democratic candidates were Lieutenant Governor of Pennsylvania [[John Fetterman]] and state representative [[Malcolm Kenyatta]].{{cite web|url=https://www.inquirer.com/columnists/attytood/john-fetterman-malcolm-kenyatta-senate-pennsyvania-20210223.html|title=It's Fetterman v. Kenyatta, for future of Pa. Dems|website=The Philadelphia Inquirer|last1=Bunch|first1=Malcolm|date=February 23, 2021|access-date=November 30, 2021}} Both Fetterman and Kenyatta were considered to be staunchly progressive Democrats, but the two men were felt to appeal to different demographics. By July 2021, Fetterman was considered the frontrunner as a result of his high name recognition and strong fundraising.{{cite web|url=https://www.goerie.com/story/news/2021/07/19/pa-senate-race-who-is-running/7994728002/|title=The race to replace Pennsylvania Sen. Pat Toomey: Here's who is running, so far|website=Erie Times-News|last1=Prose|first1=J. D.|date=July 19, 2021|access-date=November 30, 2021}} U.S. Representative [[Conor Lamb]], a [[moderate Democrat]], entered the race on August 6, 2021.{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/08/06/us/politics/conor-lamb-senate-race-pa.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20211228/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/08/06/us/politics/conor-lamb-senate-race-pa.html |archive-date=2021-12-28 |url-access=limited|title=Conor Lamb Gets In, and a Crucial Senate Fight Takes Shape in Pennsylvania|newspaper=The New York Times|last1=Gabriel|first1=Trip|date=August 6, 2021|access-date=December 7, 2021}}{{cbignore}}{{cite magazine |url=https://www.inquirer.com/politics/election/conor-lamb-philadelphia-democrats-endorsement-20220316.html |title=Philly Democrats back Conor Lamb for Senate — over the front-runner and the hometown candidate |date=March 16, 2022 |newspaper=The Philadelphia Inquirer |first=Julia |last=Terruso |access-date=April 7, 2022 |quote=solidified Lamb's status as the establishment-favored candidate }} As the campaign progressed, Lamb and Fetterman became the two most prominent candidates, with Kenyatta and [[Montgomery County Board of Commissioners|Montgomery County Commissioner]] [[Val Arkoosh]] also receiving media attention. Fetterman had maintained his frontrunner status as of December, and the other three contenders were viewed as mainly competing with each other in order to claim the anti-Fetterman mantle.{{cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2021/12/07/pennsylvania-senate-primary-test-loyal-democrat-523862|title=Senate primary tests what it means to be a loyal Democrat|website=Politico|last1=Otterbein|first1=Holly|date=December 7, 2021|access-date=December 7, 2021}} On February 4, 2022, Arkoosh withdrew from the race, her campaign having previously suffered from poor poll results and low support from party activists, leaving Kenyatta as the only major candidate from the [[Philadelphia]] region. Both Kenyatta and Lamb were considered to have a good chance at picking up voters who had previously supported Arkoosh, Lamb for ideological reasons and Kenyatta for geographical ones. In addition to Fetterman, Kenyatta, and Lamb, two minor candidates also made the Democratic primary ballot, namely Kevin Baumlin, a hospital physician, and Alexandra Khalil, a municipal official. Baumlin withdrew from the race on March 31, leaving only Khalil in addition to the three major candidates. Lamb's loss was attributed by ''[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]'' to numerous reasons, such as his not being known to voters in the [[Philadelphia metropolitan area]], where the majority of Democratic voters were located, while in contrast Fetterman's position as lieutenant governor gave him statewide name recognition. Lamb was often compared with [[conservative Democrat]]ic senators [[Joe Manchin]] and [[Kyrsten Sinema]], whom Fetterman criticized harshly. However, Lamb also criticized the Senators and said that he would vote in favor of eliminating the [[Filibuster in the United States Senate|filibuster]] in contrast to them.{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/us/pennsylvanias-moderate-democrat-lamb-distances-himself-manchin-2022-02-16/ |title=Pennsylvania's moderate Democrat Lamb distances himself from Manchin |date=February 16, 2022 |website=Reuters |first=Jarrett |last=Renshaw |access-date=May 27, 2025 |quote=Lamb has drawn comparisons to Manchin}}{{cite news |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2021/12/07/pennsylvania-senate-primary-test-loyal-democrat-523862D |title=Manchin and Sinema get star billing in Pa. Neurologists call attacks uninformed |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/republicans-suggest-john-fetterman-sick-serve-neurologists-call/story?id=89590532 |website=ABC News |access-date=23 September 2022}} In September, Oz published his medical records, which prompted Fetterman to state he was medically cleared to serve in the Senate.{{cite web |last1=Levy |first1=Marc |title=Oz releases health records to spotlight Fetterman's stroke |url=https://apnews.com/article/2022-midterm-elections-health-new-york-stroke-pennsylvania-1ac53728bd7de09c86ab2da88b94b3be |website=Associated Press |date=September 23, 2022 |access-date=23 September 2022}}{{cite web |last1=Sweitzer |first1=Justin |title=Oz's opponent, John Fetterman, says Oz's letter confirms he doesn't live in the state. Gov. John Fetterman won't participate in early-September debate with Dr. Oz |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/pittsburgh/news/lt-gov-john-fetterman-wont-participate-in-early-september-debate-with-dr-oz/ |access-date=2022-08-31 |website=CBS News |date=August 31, 2022 |language=en-US}} Fetterman attributed the delay in debating to lingering issues from his stroke and his team criticized debate concessions from Oz's team for allegedly mocking Fetterman's stroke recovery.{{Cite news |title=Fetterman rejects Oz offer to hold first debate, calls list of 'concessions' insulting |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2022-election/fetterman-rejects-oz-offer-hold-first-debate-calls-list-concessions-in-rcna45574 |access-date=2022-08-31 |work=NBC News |language=en |first=Zoë |last=Richards }} A single debate was held on October 25.{{cite news |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2022/09/07/john-fetterman-says-hell-debate-dr-oz-in-pennsylvania-senate-race-.html |title=John Fetterman says he will debate Dr. Oz as key Pennsylvania Senate race heats up |date=September 7, 2022 |work=CNBC |first=Kevin |last=Breuninger |access-date=September 8, 2022 }} ====Crudités video==== On August 15, 2022, an April 2022 campaign video of Oz shopping in a [[Redner's Markets|Redner's Warehouse]] supermarket went [[Viral video|viral]].{{cite web |title=Sen. Candidate John Fetterman Uses Dr. Oz's Viral Supermarket Gaffe to Call Out the Celebrity's Privilege |url=https://people.com/politics/john-fetterman-calls-out-dr-oz-after-viral-crudites-wegners-video/ |access-date=2022-08-16 |website=Peoplemag |language=en}} In the video, Oz says he is shopping for produce to make [[crudités]] and attributes the high prices to Democratic president [[Joe Biden]]. The video was widely ridiculed on social media and was the subject of several news articles. Most observers focused on Oz's usage of the French term "crudités", his choice of items, and several factual errors; Fetterman himself replied saying that Pennsylvanians refer to crudités as "veggie trays".{{cite web |last=Hartmann |first=Margaret |date=2022-08-15 |title=11 Questions About the Dr. Oz Crudités Video |url=https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/questions-dr-oz-crudites-video.html |access-date=2022-08-16 |website=Intelligencer |language=en-us}}{{Cite web |title=You say crudité, I say veggie platter. Fetterman vs. Oz race shows power of social media. |url=https://www.goerie.com/story/news/politics/2022/08/23/whos-winning-pa-trolling-war-between-john-fetterman-and-mehmet-oz-pa-senate-race/65410667007/ |access-date=2022-08-29 |website=Erie Times-News |language=en-US}} Oz's choice of a raw head of broccoli, asparagus, and multiple pounds of carrots, with guacamole and salsa, was criticized as wrong by some.{{cite web |last=Passy |first=Charles |title=Asparagus on the crudité tray? Here are all the mistakes Dr. Oz made in his viral grocery-store outing, according to a chef|date=August 16, 2022|url=https://www.marketwatch.com/story/here-are-all-the-mistakes-dr-oz-made-while-grocery-shopping-for-crudites-says-this-nyc-chef-11660675873 |access-date=2022-08-16 |website=MarketWatch |language=EN-US}} Others expressed confusion at Oz's statement that the $20 cost of the vegetables and dips "doesn't even include the tequila", as tequila is not a traditional accompaniment to crudités and liquor is not sold in grocery stores in Pennsylvania. Many observers noted Oz quoted the wrong price tag for the salsa and falsely suggested the broccoli was $2 per head when it was $2 per pound.{{cite web |last=Lahoda |first=Alice |title=A Complete List Of Every Bizarre Thing Dr. Oz Does In This 39-Second Clip Of Him Grocery Shopping |url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/alicelahoda/dr-oz-bizarre-grocery-store-video |access-date=2022-08-16 |website=BuzzFeed |date=August 16, 2022 |language=en}} The number of internet searches for crudités dramatically increased in the aftermath of the video's circulation. Oz appearing to confuse the Redner's and [[Wegmans]] supermarket chains led to the name "Wegner's" trending on Twitter and a parody Twitter account called "Wegner's Groceries" gaining popularity. The Fetterman campaign sought to capitalize on the video by introducing merchandise referencing it.{{cite web |date=2022-08-16 |title=John Fetterman fundraises off Dr.Oz's ad—"Let them eat crudité" |url=https://www.newsweek.com/john-fetterman-fundraises-dr-oz-adlet-them-eat-crudite-us-senate-pennsylvania-1733857 |access-date=2022-08-16 |website=Newsweek |language=en}} When asked if the video made him unrelatable to voters, Oz emphasized he helped others throughout his career and would continue to help if elected.{{cite news |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2022-election/oz-responds-viral-crudite-video-fetterman-fundraises-rcna43619 |title=Oz responds to viral crudité video after Fetterman fundraises off it |date=August 17, 2022 |work=NBC News |first=Allan |last=Smith |access-date=August 20, 2022 }} ====Debate==== In the October 25 debate, a special arrangement of transcription monitors was put in place to assist Fetterman with his auditory processing issue. According to the [[Associated Press]], Fetterman "struggled at times to explain his positions and often spoke haltingly", with Fetterman facing issues completing sentences and frequently pausing after questions were asked. Oz was described as being "more at home on the debate stage" and presented himself as a moderate Republican, and did not reference Fetterman's health condition. Independent health experts said that Fetterman was recovering "remarkably well".{{cite web |last1=Levy |first1=Marc |last2=Peoples |first2=Steve |title=Fetterman struggles in Senate debate against Oz after stroke |url=https://apnews.com/article/2022-midterm-elections-mehmet-oz-biden-health-john-fetterman-a89f9aff7d89efe43f2c40a74bbc9250 |website=[[Associated Press]] |language=en |date=October 25, 2022}} Fetterman particularly struggled answering a question regarding his previous opposition to fracking by stating he always supported fracking, while Oz answered a question on abortion by saying that the federal government should have no role in states' abortion decisions, instead leaving abortion decisions to "women, doctors, [and] local political leaders".{{cite web |last1=Terruso |first1=Julia |last2=Tamari |first2=Jonathan |title=Key takeaways from the Pa. Senate debate between John Fetterman and Mehmet Oz |url=https://www.inquirer.com/politics/election/pennsylvania-senate-debate-john-fetterman-mehmet-oz-20221027.html |website=[[Philadelphia Inquirer]] |access-date=October 26, 2022 |language=en |date=October 26, 2022}}{{cite web |last1=Manchester |first1=Julia |title=Five takeaways from the Fetterman-Oz debate in Pennsylvania |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/3704208-five-takeaways-from-the-fetterman-oz-debate-in-pennsylvania/ |website=The Hill |access-date=October 26, 2022 |date=October 26, 2022}}{{cite news |url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/10/26/politics/oz-abortion-debate-pennsylvania-senate/index.html |date=October 26, 2022 |work=CNN |first=Chris |last=Cillizza |author-link=Chris Cillizza |title=Dr. Oz's awful answer on abortion |access-date=November 1, 2022}}{{cite news |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2022/10/28/metro/oz-says-abortion-decisions-should-involve-women-doctors-local-politicians/ |newspaper=Boston Globe |first=Stephanie |last=Ebbert |title=Oz says abortion decisions should involve women, doctors – and local politicians |date=October 28, 2022 |access-date=November 1, 2022}} According to ''[[Politico]]'' and ''[[The Guardian]]'', Fetterman "struggled" during the debate, and some Democrats questioned why he chose to debate at all.{{cite web |title=Pundits divided over Fetterman's performance in key Senate debate |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2022/oct/26/fetterman-oz-debate-democrats-pennsylvania-senate |work=[[The Guardian]] |first=Ed |last=Pilkington |access-date=November 1, 2022 |language=en |date=October 26, 2022}}{{cite web |last1=Otterbein |first1=Holly |title=Fetterman struggles during TV debate with Oz debate, the Fetterman campaign claimed that the closed captioning system provided by [[Nexstar Media Group]] gave incorrect and slow captions. Undecided |- |style="text-align:left;"|[[Data for Progress]] (D){{efn-ua|name=Fetterman}} |May 7–14, 2021 |341 (LV) |± 5.3% |{{party shading/Republican}}|'''44%''' |42% |14% |} {{hidden end}} ===Results=== Fetterman won the election by 4.9 percentage points, and was declared the winner in the early hours of November 9. The early victory came as a shock to many pundits, as the race was expected to take several days to project a winner;{{cite magazine|title=The Unlikely Victory of John Fetterman|url=https://www.newyorker.com/news/news-desk/the-unlikely-victory-of-john-fetterman|date=November 9, 2022|author1=Griswold, Eliza|magazine=The New Yorker}} the race was one of the first signs of the coming Democratic overperformance relative to the final polls in the midterms writ large.{{citation needed|date=April 2024|reason="first sign" commentary is not included in the New Yorker source}} Oz underperformed former Republican president [[Donald Trump]]'s performance in the [[2020 United States presidential election in Pennsylvania]] by 3.7 percentage points, while overperforming Republican nominee [[Doug Mastriano]] in the [[2022 Pennsylvania gubernatorial election|concurrent gubernatorial race]] by 10 percentage points. With this election, a Democrat was elected to both U.S. Senate seats from Pennsylvania for the first time since [[1944 United States Senate election in Pennsylvania|1944]], and to this seat since [[1962 United States Senate election in Pennsylvania|1962]].{{efn|Democrats briefly held both of Pennsylvania's Senate seats from 2009 to 2011 when [[Arlen Specter]], who was elected as a Republican to this seat, switched to the Democratic Party.}} According to [[Ron Brownstein]] of [[CNN]] in 2023, Fetterman won independent voters by double-digit margins, which contributed to Oz's defeat.{{cite news|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/10/10/politics/fault-lines-mccarthy-trump-speakership-2024/index.html|title=McCarthy's fall and Trump's rise reflect the same bet among Republicans|publisher=CNN|last1=Brownstein|first1=Ronald|date=October 10, 2023|accessdate=October 10, 2023}} {{Election box begin | title = 2022 United States Senate election in Pennsylvania{{cite web |title=2022 General Election Official Returns – United States Senator |url=https://www.electionreturns.pa.gov/_ENR/General/OfficeResults?OfficeID=2&ElectionID=94&ElectionType=G&IsActive=0|website=Pennsylvania Department of State}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.fec.gov/documents/5675/federalelections2022.pdf|title=FEDERAL ELECTIONS 2022 Election Results for the U.S. Senate and the U.S. House of Representatives|website=www.fec.gov}} }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link | candidate = [[John Fetterman]] | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 2,751,012 | percentage = 51.17% | change = +3.88% }} {{Election box candidate with party link|candidate=[[Mehmet Oz]]|party=Republican Party (United States)|votes=2,487,260|percentage=46.27%|change=-2.45%}} {{Election box candidate with party link|candidate=Erik Gerhardt|party=Libertarian Party (United States)|votes=72,887|percentage=1.36%|change=-2.52%}} {{Election box candidate with party link|candidate=Richard L.
